column1: # Reviewed differences between the routes of the Lean proofs and those of the paper's proofs.
# One line per difference: LABEL<TAB>±OTHER<TAB>reason. TeX lines are those of arXiv:1711.10545v1;
# the result numbers are those of the published version. `*` records a use the paper makes throughout
# without citing it. Lemma 6's label (`lem::no2 3_2`) contains a space, so the route check cannot map
# it to a Lean result; its uses are not checked.

column3: Lemma 3 (a cycle of a level-1 network has one hybrid node; two cycles share at most one node) is used throughout without citation, whenever the paper speaks of the hybrid node of a cycle, the cycle C_v of a hybrid node v, or its v-blocks; the paper states it at TeX l. 346-350, citing Rosselló and Valiente.

Theorem 2 is the root library's NMSC.nmscCF_inducedNetwork, whose proof is the paper's (TeX l. 592-594: the process conditioned at LSA(s), exchangeability of the lineages there). Observation 1 enters it as NMSC.cherryMass_of_mem, on the forests of the coalescent process, so the route does not pass through observation1, which states the same fact for rooted binary trees.

The proof cites Allman, Degnan, Rhodes 2011 (TeX l. 631: their Proposition 11; published: Proposition 4) for the equality of concordance factors of species trees with the same unrooted metric tree. Proposition 4 as printed is an identifiability statement; the step uses root-placement invariance, the source's Theorem 9 and Proposition 11, stated as pub:rootplace.
See the line above: the step at TeX l. 631 uses root-placement invariance (pub:rootplace).

The proof cites Allman, Degnan, Rhodes 2011 (TeX l. 715: their Propositions 3 and 11; published: Propositions 3 and 4) for the equality of the concordance factors of T_c, T_d and ((a,b):l,(c,d):0). Propositions 3 and 4 as printed are identifiability statements; the step uses root-placement invariance (pub:rootplace).
See the line above (TeX l. 715).
See the lines above: the step at TeX l. 715 uses root-placement invariance (pub:rootplace).

The base case cites Allman, Degnan, Rhodes 2011 (TeX l. 811: their Proposition 3; published: Proposition 3) for CF(Q) = CF(Q~) when Q and Q~ are trees with the same unrooted metric tree. Proposition 3 as printed is an identifiability statement; the step uses root-placement invariance (pub:rootplace).
See the line above: the base case at TeX l. 811 uses root-placement invariance (pub:rootplace).

The paper computes the concordance factors of an unrooted quartet network, defined as those of any of its rootings (TeX l. 826, by Corollary 3 and Proposition 5); the Lean proof computes them on an explicit rooting and passes to every LSA quartet network with the same unrooted network by Proposition 5.

The induction (TeX l. 912-921) removes 2_2- and 3_1-cycles one at a time and needs the possible cycles of Q- together with a 3_2- or 4-cycle, which Lemmas 5 and 6 give; the paper does not cite them there.
As for Proposition 6: the reduction at TeX l. 964 uses Lemmas 5 and 6 for the cycles that can accompany the 3_2-cycle, without citing them.

The paper identifies the concordance factors of N on s with those of Q-_s (CF_s = CF(Q-_s), TeX l. 821, 826, 938), which is Theorem 2 with Corollary 3; the Lean statement is about N's concordance factors and passes to Q+_s by Theorem 2.

Departure from the paper (recorded in lemma13's docstring): Lemma 12 holds for generic parameters and Lemma 13 is stated for given ones (TeX l. 1108, 1111); the proof uses the direction of Lemma 12's proof that holds for all parameters, Proposition 9 and the correspondence of cycles of Q-_s and N-.

Lemma 1(iii) (LSA(Z) is below LSA(Y) when Z is a subset of Y) is used without citation where the hybrid node of the 4-cycle of Q-_s is read as a node of N- (the map psi, TeX l. 1105, used at l. 1159): a cycle of N- meeting two blocks of s lies below LSA(s).

The induction hypothesis is applied to N- restricted to S_i and s_j (Definition 10, TeX l. 1190); its concordance factors are those of N on those taxa by Proposition 1 and Theorem 2, which the paper does not cite there.

The corrected statement replaces the step by its added hypothesis.
